content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To obtain book name, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Contact the retired librarian (30 minutes)
Step 2. Receive the final title confirmation (5 minutes)
Step 3. Search the specialized digital catalog (20 minutes)
Step 4. Request access to the private collection (2 days)
Step 5. Cross-reference the author's pseudonym (1 hour)
Step 6. Wait for the archive key to be mailed (3 days)
Step 7. Travel to the university repository (4 hours)
Step 8. Scan the rare manuscript index (2 hours)
Step 9. Consult with a linguistics expert (1 hour)
Step 10. Compile the final metadata report (45 minutes)
Step 11. Post an inquiry on a literary forum (15 minutes)
Step 12. Locate the specific shelf in the basement (30 minutes)
Step 13. Apply for a temporary research permit (1 day)
Step 14. Review the librarian's personal notes (2 hours)
Step 15. Identify the vague plot description (10 minutes)
Step 16. Translate the old preface (3 hours)
Step 17. Verify the publisher's defunct records (4 hours)
Step 18. Examine the physical dust jacket fragments (1 hour)
Step 19. Sort through the librarian's correspondence (5 hours)
Step 20. Interview the estate executor (2 hours)
Step 21. Document the book's registration number (10 minutes)
Step 22. Search for the illustrator's name (40 minutes)
Step 23. Browse the restricted stack section (1 hour)
Step 24. Match the manuscript with the index entry (1 hour)
Step 25. Check the copyright office records (3 days)
Step 26. Hire a private book scout (2 days)
Step 27. Photograph the title page (5 minutes)
Step 28. Verify the ISBN history (30 minutes)
Step 29. Log the discovery in the database (15 minutes)
Step 30. Transcribe the handwritten title (15 minutes)
Step 31. Download the full digital record (10 minutes)
Step 32. Monitor the forum for expert replies (1 day)
Step 33. Authenticate the publisher's watermark (2 hours)
Step 34. Compare the fragments with the preface (1 hour)
Step 35. Inspect the binding for hidden labels (30 minutes)
Step 36. Confirm the official publication title (15 minutes)
Step 37. Request a certified extract of the record (2 days)
Step 38. Analyze the repository's acquisition log (2 hours)
Step 39. Browse the national bibliography (3 hours)
Step 40. Obtain the vault security clearance (6 hours)
